transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, what brings me in is… I just can’t seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. Like I’ll be trying to work, and one saw starts up, or someone walks past the office, or even just some thought pops in about another job I’m supposed to do, and I’m gone. Totally pulled off what I was doing.

And then—sorry, this is how it goes—I think, “Oh, I’ll just check that one thing,” and next thing I know the whole day’s gotten away from me. It’s really starting to mess with me.
Did you have this same kind of trouble focusing when you were a child?

Yeah… I mean, yes, it goes way back. In grade school, before I was 12, my teachers were always telling my mom I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, or forget what I was supposed to do after they gave instructions.

And I remember sitting there staring out the window instead of finishing the work at my desk—there was this big tree outside one classroom, and I’d just get caught up watching whatever was going on out there. But the main thing is, yeah, they were saying that stuff when I was pretty young.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or wired for several days in a row?

Um… unusually energetic for several days? I don’t know. I mean, I have days where I’m up and running around a lot, especially if there’s a job that has to get done and everything’s behind, but that’s more like… work pressure, you know?

“Wired” makes me think of too much coffee, which—actually, I used to drink this awful gas station coffee near one job site, and it would make my hands feel shaky, but that’s not really what you’re asking. I don’t think I’ve noticed a stretch of days where I felt unusually energized like that. Not that stands out to me, anyway.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I don’t know if I’d call it worry exactly. I mean, I think about things a lot—like if I measured something wrong, or if I left a tool somewhere, or whether I was supposed to call somebody back… but then again, some of that is just normal, right? In carpentry if you cut something wrong it’s not like you can un-cut it.

Sorry, I’m kind of wandering. I guess I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I sit around worrying for no reason all the time, but I do get caught up thinking about things. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Down or depressed… I’m not really sure. I mean, I have days where I’m tired of everything, like anybody does, especially when a job runs long or the weather messes up the whole schedule. Rain days can throw everything off, and then you’re sitting there thinking about all the stuff that’s piling up.

But most days? I don’t know if I’d call it depressed. I guess I haven’t really tracked it that way. What do you mean by “most days,” like all day long or just feeling low sometimes?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things?

Excessively about many different things… I don’t know. I mean, I can get stuck on stuff, like whether I forgot to bring something to a site, or if I’m going to have to go all the way back across town because I left a level sitting somewhere. That happened once—well, I thought it happened, and then it was in the truck the whole time, under a jacket.

But many different things… I’m not sure. I don’t sit there making a list of worries, exactly. It’s more like my brain jumps around to whatever I’m supposed to be keeping track of. So I guess I don’t know if I’d call it excessive worrying, or just… trying not to mess things up.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

Anxious or on edge… I’m not sure. Sometimes I’m keyed up, I guess, especially when there’s a lot going on and I’m trying to keep everything straight. But “anxious” sounds like— I don’t know, like something bigger than what I’d call it.

On a job site you kind of have to stay alert anyway. Like if someone sets a ladder in the wrong spot or there’s cords everywhere, you’re watching where you step, and then somebody asks where the screws are and I’m thinking, didn’t I just have them? Sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I don’t know if I often feel on edge. I notice it more when things are scattered or I’m behind, but I couldn’t say it’s all the time.
Do you often feel restless, like you have a hard time sitting still?

Yeah, I think so. Not like I’m pacing all day or anything, but if I have to sit at the desk and do estimates, or sit through one of those long meetings, I start feeling wound up inside. Like my body wants to get up and move around even though I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish the thing.

It’s funny, because my wrist is healed now, so it’s not like I have that excuse anymore to be getting up and fussing with stuff. But sitting there, looking at numbers or listening to someone go on and on, I get this feeling like I need to move, or shift around, or go check something. I can sit, but it feels harder than it probably should.
Do these focus problems happen in other parts of your life too, like at home, or mainly just at work?

It’s definitely not just work. Work is where it shows up loudest, I guess, because if I mess up an order or forget to schedule something, everybody knows about it. I’ve lost commissions over delays or mistakes, and then we’ve had to redo things on jobs because I missed some detail or ordered the wrong thing, and after a while the crew just… they don’t want to count on me for scheduling or ordering as much.

But at home too, yeah. My husband handles the bills now, and a lot of the reminders, because I’ll put papers somewhere “safe” and then they’re just gone. Or I miss that something needed to be done until it’s already late. I hate saying that, because I’m not trying to dump it on him, but that’s sort of what’s happened.
